name: Chakuli Pitha
steps: Wash and soak rice and urad dal separately for 5 hours. Drain and grind with the measured water to a smooth batter slightly thicker than ordinary dosa batter.
Cover loosely and ferment overnight until expanded and bubbly. Fold in salt gently; leave the batter airy instead of beating it flat.
Heat a lightly oiled griddle over medium heat. Pour a ladleful and spread into a medium round, thinner than an uttapam but not paper-thin.
Cover for about 2 minutes until the top shows pores and sets. Flip briefly for 30–45 seconds, keeping the pitha soft with pale golden patches; repeat to make eight.
Serve two warm chakuli pithas per person with coconut chutney. The fermentation and soft texture distinguish them from instant flour crepes.
tips: Let the batter ferment sufficiently; under-fermented batter cooks dense.
passiveTime: Soak rice and dal for 5 hours; ferment overnight.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
